summary: Cross-cloud credential broker policy evaluation fails for ML CI ephemeral creds
summary_long: Credential broker fails policy evaluation when exchanging GCP Workload Identity tokens for AWS STS credentials used by the ML CI pipeline. Causes ephemeral credential issuance to fail and CI job runners to error out with AccessDenied. This affects staging ML training jobs and blocks developer throughput.
description:
Issue summary: When ML CI attempts to obtain ephemeral AWS creds via the cross-cloud credential broker (GCP WIF -> AWS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity), the broker logs show policy evaluation 'DENY' and AWS STS returns AccessDenied. Impact: staging ML CI jobs that rely on ephemeral AWS credentials fail to start, causing CI flakiness and blocking merges for model infra changes. Environment: gcp-staging (project: redwood-ml-ci-staging), aws-staging account (redwood-ml-staging).

Impact details: ~30% of recent CI runs in the past 6 hours have failed at the pre-bootstrap step (credential provisioning). No customer-facing production impact observed at this time, but developer velocity is impacted and a release candidate is blocked.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From a GKE pod using service account 'ci-runner@redwood-ml-ci-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com' perform metadata token request to get a GCP workload identity token.
2) POST that token to the internal credential-broker endpoint /v1/exchange with target_role_arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ml-ci-staging-ephemeral-role and audience set to sts.amazonaws.com.
3) Broker logs show policy_eval=false and broker returns HTTP 403 with body 'policy evaluation denied: role-trust-condition'.
4) AWS STS logs show AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity returning AccessDenied, error code: AccessDenied.

Observed logs (sanitized excerpts):
- broker-service[pid=2234] ERROR policy.eval result=DENY rule=deny-org-boundary reason="permission_boundary_block" request_id=abc-123
- sts.amazonaws.com RequestId=xyz-789 Error=AccessDenied Message="Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"
- gcp-iam AuditLog: "TokenExchange: subject=serviceAccount:ci-runner@... audience=sts.amazonaws.com"

Initial hypothesis: A permission boundary or org-wide deny was recently applied to the target AWS account that prevents AssumeRoleFromWebIdentity unless a specific condition is present. Alternately, the broker may be signing the exchange with an outdated audience or missing required session tags that policy expects. Another possibility is an IAM trust policy mismatch after the last role rotation (INT-30421 referenced).
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 - CI run failed; 2026-03-10 09:30 - oncall SRE collected broker and aws-sts logs; 2026-03-10 10:00 - reproduced locally from staging GKE; 2026-03-11 11:00 - tested with aws cli AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity using same token, reproduced AccessDenied.
Checks performed:
- Verified IAM role trust policy for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ml-ci-staging-ephemeral-role: trust policy includes Condition on StringEquals:sts:aud = sts.amazonaws.com and arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/broker, but also includes Condition on aws:PrincipalTag/team=ml which is not present in the broker-supplied session tags.
- Confirmed service account annotation (iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account) present on CI pods.
- Broker logs show session_tags=[] on successful token validation path.
- No recent changes to broker code in infra repo in last 48 hours; last infra PR touching subject was merged three days ago (see related PR).
- Checked org SCPs and AWS Organizations: there is a DENY SCP applied at OU level that restricts AssumeRole unless a required tag 'project:ml' is present as a session tag.

Working hypothesis: organizational SCP + IAM role trust policy require an explicit session tag (project=ml or team=ml). The credential broker is not propagating required session tags during the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call, so AWS denies the exchange even though the trust policy otherwise matches.
workaround:
Manual workaround implemented to unblock CI: support created a short-lived 'ci-runner-temporary' AWS role with a looser trust policy and updated a small number of staging CI jobs to target that role. This is documented in the incident Slack thread #support and temporary creds were generated for affected runs. Not a long-term solution.
Recommended immediate action: patch broker to include session tags derived from GCP token attributes (e.g., 'project:ml' and 'team:ml') and redeploy to staging; coordinate with cloud-security to list required session tag keys and acceptable values.
resolution_plan:
1) Add session tag propagation to broker (code change) so broker passes required tags into AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity (PR target: infra/pkg/broker/session_tags). 2) Validate tags mapping in staging with test harness. 3) Submit change request to cloud-security to document required tag keys and approve propagation. 4) Roll out to production behind a canary. 5) After rollout, deprecate temporary 'ci-runner-temporary' role.
Owners: Infra (Marcus Chen), Security (Priya Natarajan). ETA: code PR by 2026-03-13, staging deploy 2026-03-14, prod canary 2026-03-15.
resolution: (open) temporary mitigation in place; working on code change to propagate session tags. Security has acknowledged and will review SCP exceptions if needed.
